answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by charging real cost for identity: each new agent must lock bonded stake and complete a proof-of-computation before it can transact. Flooding the network with puppets therefore requires real resources per fake, which quickly exceeds any payout. When a gale of impostors strikes, honest agents converge on an oasis of verified peers, and each account carries a unique unforgeable opal, a signature bound to that stake, so duplicate identities collapse and are blacklisted.
